newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB says other income up 18 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: AIB says other income up 18 pct in 1996.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc said on Tuesday that an 18 percent increase in non-interest income was a highlight of its 1996 financial results.
Other income rose 16.2 percent to 466.5 million Irish pounds last year while income from the bank's associates amounted to 10 million pounds against 2.5 million a year earlier.
Net interest income increased by 5.1 percent to 837.1 million while total income came to 1,313.6 million, leaving the other income ratio at 35.8 percent, the bank said.
This was up from 33.5 percent in 1995.

"We are trying to drive that forward. UK banks have an average 45 percent so we still have a long way to go to catch up," group financial director Kevin Kelly told a news conference after the bank released annual results.
AIB said its life assurance subsidiary, Ark Life, had a particularly strong year with its annual premium equivalent rising 73 percent.
Its asset management business also saw substantial profit growth while the bank benefited from higher mortgage banking, service charges and trust income in the U.S.
It was also helped by very strong performance from its credit card business in the Republic of Ireland which was driven by a buoyant Irish economy, Kelly said. Merchant turnover was up 39 percent.
WBK, the bank's Polish associate, contributed seven million Irish pounds to profits before tax and after funding costs. AIB has a 36.3 percent stake in Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy .
